intro.title: Build centralized error handler middleware
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a centralized error handler middleware for a Node.js application. You'll learn how to create a function that catches errors from your routes and processes them in one place, making your code cleaner and more maintainable. The core concept involves using Express middleware and JavaScript's error handling constructs like try-catch and custom error objects. You'll work with Node.js, Express, and middleware functions to implement this essential backend pattern.
intro.usecase: Centralized error handling is essential in production Node.js applications like e-commerce platforms, banking systems, and SaaS dashboards. For example, when a payment form submission fails in an online store, a centralized handler can catch the error, log it for debugging, and return a user-friendly message instead of crashing the server. In analytics dashboards, this middleware ensures that API errors from data-fetching endpoints are consistently formatted and logged, maintaining system stability while providing clear feedback to users. Developers implement this pattern to prevent server crashes, standardize error responses across all routes, and simplify debugging in complex applications.
